purpose: Define repository-level evidence/history semantics that extend the Prompt Kit ontology without treating preference, critique, transport metadata, or declared proof ceilings as observed runtime proof.

invocation.description: A concrete attempt to invoke an implementation. Invocation alone does not prove success.

run_result.description: Observed result of an invocation, bound to the exact subject and evidence source.

failure.description: Observed failure or regression. A failure may reduce or block a claim but can never raise proof.

critique.description: Review or critique signal. It becomes proof only through separate validating evidence.

favorite.description: User preference signal. Favorites are discoverability/utility evidence, not correctness proof.

feedback.description: Explicit user feedback signal. Transport and private payload handling remain owned by the feedback subsystem.

eval.description: Executable evaluation result with an oracle, fixture, or acceptance rule tied to the observed subject.

proof_receipt.description: Immutable receipt binding an observed claim to exact subject identity, evidence, and proof ceiling.

proof_ceiling: Static repository contract and validator proof only. This contract does not assert that any invocation, run, failure, critique, favorite, feedback event, eval, or proof receipt has actually occurred.
